Design (fixed before the run): compared labs of 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24 against field-wide OSO at α = 0.8 and 0.2, by budget · held the same: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7), 24 identical agents, budget 75 split equally, no mint, no validation · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 30 graphs × 5 runs on each, per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

The simple model with 24 identical agents on the default graph (deeper ideas harder by 2 bits per level), 6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, composition 0.7; each graph run 5 times. Traditional rules (α = 1, nothing published before a target), with agents in equal labs of 1 (alone), 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 or 24 (one lab of everyone); lab mates share every proof at once, privately. Against OSO across the whole field at α = 0.8 and 0.2. Held fixed: equal money per agent every round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation.
